reference_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per order of a known customer
  SELECT customer_id, channel,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_ts DESC, order_id) AS rn
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY channel
alternatives:
WITH latest AS (  -- one row per known customer
  SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_ts) AS order_ts
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
latest_ids AS (  -- one row per known customer
  SELECT o.customer_id, MIN(o.order_id) AS order_id
  FROM orders o
  JOIN latest l ON l.customer_id = o.customer_id AND l.order_ts = o.order_ts
  GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT o.channel, COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM latest_ids li
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = li.order_id
GROUP BY o.channel

SELECT t.channel, COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM (
  -- one row per order of a known customer, numbered from the latest
  SELECT customer_id, channel,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_ts DESC, order_id) AS rn
  FROM orders
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
) AS t
WHERE t.rn = 1
GROUP BY t.channel

FROM latest_ids li

other_way.tradeoff: The latest time per customer, then the lowest order_id at it, needs no window but takes two grouping steps and a join back.
